title: The Czech National Bank raised all three rates by 25 basis points
summary: The Czech National Bank’s 5 November decision raised the two-week repo rate to 4.00%, the discount rate to 3.00% and the Lombard rate to 5.00%. Each moved up by 25 basis points. The repo rate therefore remained at the midpoint of a two-percentage-point corridor. The terms changed the level at which the three instruments operated while preserving the distance between them.

All three rates took effect on 6 November. The dated decision notice records the instrument settings and effective date. It links separately to the Board’s press-conference statement, presentation, Q&A and meeting minutes. Investors assessing the surprise on announcement day need the prior expected rate and the timing of the initial release. The notice itself gives neither, and the vote and reasoning belong to the separately identified documents.

questions.question: How much of the 25-basis-point increase was unexpected?
questions.detail: Use timestamped CNB announcement records and pre-release CZK overnight-indexed swap quotes to establish the event window and expected repo setting. An instrument spanning 6 November will contain days at the old and new rates. Account for that split before estimating the surprise.

questions.question: Did short rates and the koruna react to the decision or to the subsequent explanation?
questions.detail: Compare synchronised executable rates and FX quotes around the confirmed decision timestamp, then around the press-conference statement and Q&A. Common European rate or currency moves in the same interval can distort the attribution. The decision notice on its own establishes no market reaction.

questions.question: How closely did overnight market rates follow the parallel shift?
questions.detail: Compare the official overnight reference rate and trading volumes immediately before and after the 6 November effective date. The corridor kept the same width, so a change in the market rate’s distance from the repo midpoint would warrant checking liquidity conditions and use of standing facilities.
